name: RenewScope – Subscription Renewal Diagnostics for WooCommerce
author: hailunmicrosaas

sections.description:
Seeing failed Stripe renewal payments in WooCommerce Subscriptions? RenewScope reads your store’s own records and tells you, in plain language, what looks wrong and where to look next, without changing anything.

You’ll need WooCommerce, an active compatible WooCommerce Subscriptions integration, and WooCommerce Stripe Payment Gateway for the full set of checks. WooCommerce is needed to open the tool. If Subscriptions or Stripe is missing, checks that depend on it are marked unavailable and the remaining checks still run. See Compatibility below before relying on subscription findings.

It is a local diagnostic tool, not a payment repair service. A warning can mean missing information, not necessarily a broken payment. An OK result covers only the information checked; it does not prove that payments, webhooks or scheduled tasks work.

What you get

  • Review saved Stripe settings and renewal background tasks for things that need attention.
  • Review failed renewal orders created in the last 30 and 90 days, separating active failures from older invoices with a later observed payment.
  • See recognized Stripe failure reasons, unpaid renewals waiting for payment, previously failed orders now paid, and on-hold subscriptions linked to an unpaid failure.
  • See incomplete or unavailable checks clearly instead of treating missing information as a healthy zero.
  • Copy a redacted text report for support. No report history is saved.

Use findings as a checklist to review; don’t retry payments or change fraud settings just to make a warning go away.

What it doesn’t do

  • It doesn’t contact Stripe, so it can’t confirm that a card was actually charged or that Stripe is working.
  • It recognizes only a limited set of saved English Stripe payment-failure messages. Translated or custom messages can leave the reason unknown rather than guessed.
  • It can’t tell whether a retry used the same card.
  • It doesn’t identify failures caused by a closed Stripe Link account. Stripe Link is Stripe’s saved-payment service; this limit does not mean all Link payments are ignored.
  • The 30-day and 90-day numbers overlap, so don’t add them together.

Compatibility

Tested on selected WordPress 6.2–7.1 and WooCommerce 8.2–11.3 installations. These are the tested combinations, not a promise that every pairing or customization works:

  • WordPress 7.1.4 with WooCommerce 11.2.2, WooCommerce Stripe Payment Gateway 11.1.1 or 11.2.0, PHP 8.4.24 and the open-source WooCommerce Subscriptions core 8.2.0. This setup was also tested with simulated subscriptions separately. A basic check run also passed on WooCommerce 11.3.0.
  • WordPress 6.9.11 with WooCommerce 11.0.1, WooCommerce Stripe Payment Gateway 10.0.1 and PHP 8.4.24. Subscriptions were simulated in these tests.
  • WordPress 6.2.15 with WooCommerce 8.2.5 and PHP 7.4.33 or 8.4.24. Subscriptions were simulated; Stripe was not installed because the Stripe plugin needs a newer WordPress version.

Both legacy order storage and High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS) were checked on MariaDB. The newest setup also covered HPOS with synchronization off and on.

Failure reasons and the saved Link and Express checkout settings are checked only on WooCommerce Stripe Payment Gateway 10.0.1, 11.1.1, 11.1.2 and 11.2.0. On other Stripe versions those rows are marked “not checked” and the other checks still run. Block reasons are not checked on 10.0.1. Version 11.1.2 was checked against its published source code; it is not in the tested setups listed above.

Not yet tested with the current paid WooCommerce Subscriptions plugin. Simulated subscriptions do not establish compatibility with that plugin, its automatic retries or its full renewal lifecycle. Confirm compatibility on a staging copy before relying on these results.

The open-source core 8.2.0 is an archived library used in testing, not a maintained replacement for the paid plugin. It is not included here. Core-only installations have no automatic retry settings for this tool to check.

WooCommerce and Stripe names identify integrations only; this plugin is independent of and not endorsed by either company.

Privacy

Checks are read-only and no data leaves the site through this plugin’s requests. There are no Stripe API calls, analytics, telemetry or remotely loaded scripts, fonts or images. Optional documentation links open only when you choose them.

The plugin saves no settings or reports of its own and adds no background jobs. Results last only while you view the page. Deleting the plugin requires no cleanup of its own saved data; it does not delete your store’s records.

Findings contain counts and general explanations, with version information and dates for support. The report replaces site identity with [redacted]. No customer details, card data, record IDs, payment references or raw notes are shown or exported.

Copy report copies the displayed report to your clipboard. Review it before sharing. No report is sent or stored by the plugin.
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins > Add New Plugin (Add New on older WordPress versions), search for RenewScope, then select Install Now and Activate. To install from a ZIP file instead, select Upload Plugin on the same screen, choose the RenewScope ZIP, then select Install Now and Activate.
  2. Go to WooCommerce > RenewScope. Use an administrator or shop manager account with permission to manage WooCommerce.
  3. Select Run checks. Results show on the same page.
  4. If you need help, select Copy report before leaving. Reports aren’t saved.

There’s nothing to set up in this plugin. Your WooCommerce and payment integrations need to be installed and active separately.
sections.faq:
Does this fix failed payments or trigger retries?

No. It never changes settings, orders, subscriptions, notes, payment methods, schedules or retry records. Suggested next steps are for manual review.

Why are subscription checks unavailable?

This can happen when WooCommerce Subscriptions isn’t active, or this tool can’t confirm that the installed version is supported. It doesn’t mean you have zero failures. Check Plugins > Installed Plugins, and copy the report if you ask WooCommerce Subscriptions support or post in this plugin’s support forum on WordPress.org. Other independent checks can still run.

Does a live-mode setting mean payments work?

No. It only reads the saved setting. It also can’t confirm your scheduled renewals actually ran or whether Stripe Link is available at checkout.

Where should I investigate a finding?

Start with Recent renewals when available. Open WooCommerce > Orders, select a renewal order and review Order notes and the linked subscription. For delayed or historical failed tasks, open WooCommerce > Status > Scheduled Actions. Historical task failures may be old or resolved; they are not necessarily card declines or urgent unpaid renewals.

For “Later payment observed — older invoice not confirmed paid”, review the older order before contacting the customer. A newer paid renewal was found for every subscription linked to that failed order. This does not prove that the older invoice was paid. An on-hold subscription’s association with a failed renewal does not prove why it was put on hold.

What do the labels mean?

OK: nothing wrong found in what was checked. Warning: something looks off, or couldn’t be fully checked. Problem: the store’s records show something that needs review, such as several failed renewals or delayed background tasks. “At least” numbers mean the check couldn’t see everything, so there may be more than shown.

Counts are orders, not customers or payment attempts. Windows use order creation dates and current statuses: an older order that failed recently can be outside them. Failure-reason groups can include unpaid orders in different statuses, so they need not match the active-failure count. These numbers are not a payment success rate.

Why might a finding be incomplete?

On very large stores the check reads only a limited number of records and aims to finish in a few seconds. If it stops early, results say “at least” and are marked incomplete. That alone doesn’t mean your store is broken. Another plugin’s slow response can make the check take longer. Missing or unreadable records can also leave gaps.

Some saved messages aren’t recognized, and the tool can’t confirm a retry used the same card. It does not use Subscriptions’ written notes to identify renewals. For support, the exact coverage limits are:

  • WooCommerce Subscriptions notes are not used; subscription detection uses structured local data.
  • Link-closed failures: not covered.
  • Same-method payment history cannot be confirmed.

Can I use it without JavaScript?

Yes. Run checks and select the read-only report text manually. Use Ctrl+C on Windows/Linux or Command+C on Mac. The Copy report button uses your local clipboard only after you click it; it does not send a report anywhere.
